note:
Runner: service/test/auth-reachability.test.ts. Runners are ordinary risk; this file is the truth. A-001, A-002 and A-003 must FAIL against the tree at 0036c74 -- a defect spec proves itself by failing before (lessons/L-006). The remaining four are green on both sides on purpose: they are the claim that nothing else moved, and a claim that cannot fail is decoration, so each names the deliberate mutation that turns it red and the implementation report records that mutation being run. 'hub-less deps' throughout means AppDeps built with calendars: undefined, which is what server.ts:114 and worker.ts:244 produce when GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID or GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET is unset. Error sentences are asserted as the rendered

text, not the whole document: every page ships the same stylesheet and that stylesheet contains the comment '/* slots and calendar */' (spec/0006 S2b). A-003's redness before the fix is of a different kind from A-001's and A-002's and is spelt out on the case: nothing is unguarded today, but the calendar gate answers first, so the guards underneath it are unobservable until it is gone. AMENDED 2026-08-31 (v1.1.0), in the open, after the freeze and after a cited code-review objection (reviews/20260831-111314-code-gemini.md, citing CHARTER Part 3 requirement 2). No case, clause, step or assertion changed; the amendment is to the RUNNER's setup helper and is recorded here because the charter's freeze covers the runner too and this file is where a reader meets it. What changed: makeOrg() resolved the org it had just created with `SELECT org_id FROM orgs ORDER BY created_at DESC`. These deps freeze now(), so two orgs created inside one test carry the same created_at and the ordering is not a tiebreak -- the helper returned the FIRST org, whose admin is a different owner, and A-003's frozen step 'create an org AND configure its OIDC SSO' then failed at 404 'No such team.' before it could assert anything. It now resolves through the creating owner's own admin membership in org_members. This is exactly the L-006 shape the suite exists to respect: a lookup that is right until a second row exists, and that would have made A-003 pass or fail on row order rather than on the behaviour it names. Re-reviewed cross-family before the code review was re-taken.

deployments.MS_ONLY: hub-less; TOKEN_KEY=$KEY, MS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=ms-cid, MS_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=ms-csec; no GOOGLE_OAUTH_* at all
deployments.IDP_ONLY: hub-less; TOKEN_KEY=$KEY; no GOOGLE_OAUTH_*, no MS_OAUTH_*
deployments.NO_KEY: hub-less; no TOKEN_KEY, no GOOGLE_OAUTH_*, MS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=ms-cid, MS_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=ms-csec
deployments.GOOGLE_ID_ONLY: hub-less; TOKEN_KEY=$KEY, GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=cid and NO GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET -- so no hub is built
deployments.HUB_OTHER_KEY: calendars: new CalendarHub({}, $OTHER_KEY); config TOKEN_KEY=$KEY, MS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=ms-cid, MS_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=ms-csec -- the hub's seal key is NOT config.tokenKey

cases.description: Microsoft sign-in works end to end on a deployment with Microsoft credentials and no Google Calendar. FAILS before the fix.

steps.assert: $start.status == 303 -- before the fix this is 404 'Microsoft sign-in is not configured.'
$start.location host is login.microsoftonline.com and carries a non-empty 'state' query parameter (S2d: same microsoftSsoUrl as today)
$start.location scope parameter is unchanged from today's: openid, email, profile -- no scope is enlarged
$p is defined and $p.purpose == 'sso_ms' (S4c: the state is sealed under the deployment's own key, not emitted unsigned)
$start.state does not decode as plain base64 or base64url JSON
new OAuthState($OTHER_KEY).open($start.state) is undefined

steps.call: create an owner ms-user@example.com by invite on this same deployment

steps.with: Microsoft token endpoint stubbed to return an id_token for ms-user@example.com

steps.assert: $cb.status == 303 and $cb.location == '/app'
the set-cookie session from $cb loads GET /app with status 200 -- the whole round trip completes, not just the redirect

cases.turns_red_if: the entry point is reverted to gating on deps.calendars

cases.description: Per-org OIDC SSO works end to end on a deployment with no Google Calendar. FAILS before the fix. Fixes both paths, because the Workers build reaches this route by forwarding into the Durable Object that runs this same handle().

steps.call: sign up an org admin by invite, create org 'Corp', configure OIDC SSO for issuer https://idp.corp.example and email domain corp.example

steps.assert: $steer.status == 303 and $steer.location == '/login/sso/$orgId' -- domain steering is unchanged and it points at the route under test
$start.status == 303 -- before the fix this is 404 'SSO is not configured on this deployment.'
$start.location starts with https://idp.corp.example/authorize and carries a non-empty 'state' (S3d: discovery and redirect unchanged)
$p is defined, $p.purpose == 'oidc', $p.org == $orgId (S4c)
$start.state does not decode as plain base64 or base64url JSON, and does not open under $OTHER_KEY

steps.with: the IdP token endpoint stubbed to mint an id_token for worker@corp.example

steps.assert: $cb.status == 303 and the session it sets loads GET /app with status 200
owners.provisioned_by for worker@corp.example == 'sso:$orgId' -- JIT provisioning inside the org still happens
$aliasStart.status == 303 -- the 'main' tenant alias, which is the path the Workers router forwards as (worker.ts:805), works on this deployment too (S4e)

cases.turns_red_if: the entry point is reverted to gating on deps.calendars

cases.description: Each door still refuses when its own configuration is missing, and the refusals stay distinguishable. Partly RED before the fix -- not because a guard is missing today, but because on a hub-less deployment the calendar gate pre-empts the org-level refusals entirely, so they cannot be observed at all until it is gone. This case is the assertion that removing that gate did not remove them with it.

steps.assert: $r1.status == 404 and its error sentence is exactly 'Microsoft sign-in is not configured.' -- TOKEN_KEY alone does not open the Microsoft door
$r2.status == 404 and its error sentence is exactly 'This organization has no SSO configured.'

steps.call: GET /login/sso/main with no orgs in the database

steps.assert: $r3.status == 404 and its error sentence is exactly 'This organization has no SSO configured.'

steps.call: create an org with NO org_sso row, then GET /login/sso/<that orgId>

steps.assert: $r4.status == 404 and its error sentence is exactly 'This organization has no SSO configured.' -- an org that exists but has not configured SSO is still refused
$r5.status == 404 and its error sentence is exactly 'Microsoft sign-in is not configured.' (S2b: identical to worker.ts:614's answer)

steps.call: create an org AND configure its OIDC SSO, then GET /login/sso/<that orgId>

steps.assert: $r6.status == 404 and its error sentence is exactly 'SSO is not configured on this deployment.' (S3b, S3c: the deployment check stays above the org lookup and keeps its wording)
$r6 emits no Location header and no state at all -- with no seal key nothing unsigned is produced as a fallback

cases.turns_red_if: the msClientId term is dropped from the Microsoft guard, or the org_sso row check is dropped, or the deployment check is moved below the org lookup
cases.red_before_because: on MS_ONLY and NO_KEY (hub-less) every /login/sso/<orgId> answer today is 'SSO is not configured on this deployment.', so the steps expecting 'This organization has no SSO configured.' are red before the fix

cases.description: Google sign-in, calendar connect and the calendar callback keep exactly the reachability they have today. Nothing outside this spec's two doors moves.

steps.assert: $g1.status == 404 and its error sentence is exactly 'Google sign-in is not configured.' -- a client id without a secret is not a configured Google sign-in, and this spec does not change that
$g2.status == 404 and its error sentence is exactly 'Google sign-in is not configured.'

steps.call: POST /auth/google/start with GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET set

steps.assert: $g3.status == 303 to accounts.google.com -- with a hub it still works, unchanged

steps.call: sign in an owner, then POST /app/calendar/google/connect with that session

steps.assert: $c1 is byte-for-byte today's answer: status 200 rendering the owner's own dashboard ('Your schedules'), no Location header, and no occurrence of accounts.google.com anywhere in the body. The route is guarded by `&& deps.calendars` in its own condition (app.ts:2661), so on a hub-less deployment it does not match and the request falls through to the /app view -- verified against the tree at 0036c74, not assumed. This spec does not touch it.

steps.call: GET /oauth/google/callback?code=c&state=<a state sealed by this deployment with purpose 'calendar-ish' payload {owner_id, level}>

steps.assert: $c2.status == 404 and its error sentence is exactly 'Calendar integration is not configured.' -- spec/0006 S2d's message and placement are untouched

cases.turns_red_if: the /auth/google/start guard is changed to !states || !config.googleClientId, or the calendar route's deps.calendars guard is loosened, or spec/0006 S2d's calendar 404 is moved or reworded

cases.description: A deployment with a hub is unchanged, including one whose hub holds a key that did not come from config.tokenKey -- the state must be sealed by the sealer that will be asked to open it.

steps.assert: $start.status == 303 with a non-empty state
the hub's own state facility opens $start.state and yields purpose == 'sso_ms'
new OAuthState($KEY).open($start.state) is undefined -- config.tokenKey did NOT seal it (S1b)
$cb.status == 303 to /app -- the state opens on the way back, which is the regression this case exists for

steps.call: the same round trip for /login/sso/<orgId> on this deployment

steps.assert: it completes exactly as it does today

the full existing suites pass unchanged and unedited: test/frontdoor.test.ts, test/enterprise.test.ts, test/video.test.ts, test/oauth-state.test.ts and every other runner, with no edit to any frozen acceptance file

cases.turns_red_if: the sealer is built as oauthState(config) instead of deps.calendars?.state ?? oauthState(config)

cases.description: The Workers router is not modified. Its Microsoft door was never Google-gated and is already explicitly right; editing it and calling this item done closes nothing.

steps.assert: src/worker.ts contains the exact guard 'if (!states || !config.msClientId) {' for /auth/microsoft/start
src/worker.ts contains the exact guard 'if (!states || !config.googleClientId) {' for /auth/google/start
src/worker.ts contains no occurrence of the identifier 'CalendarHub' in its router-level state handling, and no router guard reads deps.calendars
src/worker.ts still forwards /login/sso/<tag> into the Durable Object as '/login/sso/main' -- the route is not reimplemented at the router (S4e)
git diff of this change touches src/worker.ts zero times

cases.turns_red_if: worker.ts's Microsoft or Google guard is edited, or the sso route is reimplemented at the router
